SMTO-CFG-0002 — This SMTO version can't open your saved data

GUID: 4a35ead4-b779-446f-8c09-724ad0586dba
Slug: storage-schema-version-incompatible
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • Your saved data was made by a newer SMTO, or by an old version this one no longer supports, so SMTO stopped while starting. Your data wasn't changed or deleted.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On the startup screen, open Technical details and see whether it says your data is newer than this SMTO or is no longer supported. That tells you whether you need a newer SMTO or the older one that last used this data.
  2. If the data is newer, install the SMTO version you used before (or a later one), then start SMTO again. Data saved by a newer SMTO can only be opened by that version or a later one.
  3. If the data is no longer supported, ask the person who installed SMTO to back up the data folder and start SMTO with a new, empty one. A fresh folder lets this version start, while the backup keeps your old conversations safe for a matching version.

What success looks like

  • The startup screen reaches Ready.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details on the startup screen and send them to the person who installed SMTO. Don't delete or reset the data folder, and don't copy old data files into a new folder; that can lose your conversations.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A local SQLite store's schema version metadata is missing (an unversioned pre-baseline database) or outside this build's supported range (below the minimum or newer than current), so startup stopped before any migration or write.

What this means

  • An existing database lacks required store-version metadata or its stored version lies below the supported minimum or above this build's current version. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • An existing database lacks required store-version metadata or its stored version lies below the supported minimum or above this build's current version.

How to diagnose it

  • Read the reported store/version range and preserve the entire original state; an unversioned existing database is not a fresh empty one.

How to fix it

  • Read the store name, stored version and supported range from the error or the storage_issue diagnostic. Run a build whose supported range includes that version against the preserved AOR_AGENT_STATE_DIR, or use the supported restore/import workflow; if neither applies, back up the directory and point AOR_AGENT_STATE_DIR at a fresh SMTO state directory, and never copy old database files into the fresh directory.
  • Back up the existing state directory, then start with a fresh SMTO state directory, or use a matching older runtime. Do not copy old database files into the fresh directory. The files were not migrated or deleted.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A matching supported build opens preserved state, or a deliberately separate fresh state directory initializes successfully.

What not to do

  • Do not overwrite the original state with an incompatible version; use the supported upgrade path.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
